extracted.intended_audience: faculty and researchers preparing NIH grant applications (e.g., R01, R21, R03, SBIR/STTR) seeking guidance on the NIH peer review process
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the NIH peer review process, the review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications, associated procedural requirements, summary statements, and planning for resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocating for Review / Administrative Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow administrative guidance (SPS and NIH SF424) and be direct about the connection between your research and the mission/goals of the targeted IC; use PHS Assignment Request Form and NIH Assisted Referral Tool; consider conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with ALL guidelines so your grant is not administratively rejected; talk to Program Officers; be direct about the connection between your research and the mission/goals of your targeted IC. Use PHS Assignment Request and NIH referral tools to influence appropriate assignment; consider COI when requesting assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Assignments (minimum reviewers & basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal is assigned a minimum of 3 reviewers based on scientific content, reviewer expertise, and conflict-of-interest considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study Section or SRO recruits qualified reviewers, manages conflicts of interest, and ensures a fair and objective review. Reviewers are selected to match scientific content and avoid COI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which Applications Are Discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately the top 50% of proposals (by initial triage) are discussed in study section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study section is a ~9 hour day of review; each discussed proposal gets ~13–14 minutes. During discussion reviewers with conflicts leave the room; assigned reviewers present initial scores and discuss strengths/weaknesses; open discussion follows; assigned reviewers then present final score. Voting may show 'out of range' indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria (individual scores considered in Overall Impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance; Approach; Innovation; Investigator(s); Environment — each scored individually and considered in the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored Criteria: 1 = exceptional; 9 = poor. FOA/PA/RFA may add questions to each scored criterion or additional scored criteria. Review the specific FOA for which criteria apply. These individual criterion scores feed into the overall impact (priority) score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: An overall impact (priority) score summarizes the reviewers' assessment of the likelihood the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact expressed as a score (used to calculate percentiles where applicable). Summary statements convey the overall impact; reviewers write an 'Overall Impact' paragraph summarizing strengths and weaknesses. Priority/Impact scores and percentiles are communicated to applicants (e.g., within days of meeting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scoring uses a 1–9 scale where 1 = exceptional and 9 = poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sent to reviewers and guides discussion; format for critiques in the summary statement. Reviewers assign numeric scores to the scored criteria and an overall impact score according to this scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (considered in overall score but not scored separately)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items reviewers evaluate and consider when determining scientific and technical merit, but do not give separate scores for: Study Timeline (clinical trials), Protections for Human Subjects, Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children, Vertebrate Animals, Biohazards, Resubmission, Renewal, Revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAR & RFA may add new criteria or questions to each additional item. Although not individually scored, these considerations can affect the overall impact determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations (not scored individually and not part of overall score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative/other items reviewers note but do not individually score or include in the overall impact: Applications from Foreign Organizations, Select Agents, Resource Sharing Plans, Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, Budget & Period of Support, Provision of Family Care Facilities, Recruitment & Retention Plan to Enhance Diversity, Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are considered as review 'considerations' and some may be required by FOA; they are not given separate numeric scores and are not part of the overall impact calculation, but deficiencies can still be flagged in summary statements or affect funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials–Specific Review Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For Clinical Trials applications certain criteria are emphasized or required (e.g., Study Timeline, required protections for human subjects, inclusion policies, specific CT-related questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different FOAs/mechanisms indicate whether CTs are allowed/required (slides list R01 CT Not Allowed / R01 CT Required, etc.). Clinical trial applications often require additional CT-specific review of timelines and protections; review groups and FOAs will specify exact expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Section Role and Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Study Sections (Scientific Review Groups) evaluate and make recommendations based on review criteria, provide priority scores (or 'not discussed') and written critiques (summary statements), but do NOT make funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO ensures objective and fair initial peer review; special emphasis panels may be formed ad hoc. Assigned reviewers present critiques; open discussion ensues; final scores reflect the group's judgment. Study sections recruit reviewers, handle COI, and report scores and written critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement Content and Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary Statement, written by the SRO and containing reviewers' critiques, summarizes strengths and weaknesses, highlights areas of concurrence and disagreement, and includes individual criterion scores and the overall impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides feedback for applicants; contains RESUME AND SUMMARY OF DISCUSSION, CRITIQUE(s) with per-criterion scores (e.g., Significance: 3, Approach: 4), and the Overall Impact paragraph from individual reviewers. Summary statements are privileged communications and are released to applicants after review (example: within 30 days of meeting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Level Review / Advisory Council Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: National advisory councils or boards review IC funding plans, applications, and summary statements from peer review; they consider Institute/Center goals and needs and advise IC Directors regarding funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory councils are composed of scientific and public representatives chosen by the IC. Their recommendations, together with SRG recommendations, inform the IC Director's final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Funding Decision by Institute/Center Director
rubrics_metrics.description: IC Directors make the final funding decision and typically only applications recommended by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC Director weighs peer review, advisory council advice, and IC goals/needs in making funding decisions. Applicants may be funded only after favorable outcome from both levels where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications & Timeline (post-submission milestones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical administrative timeline items include notification of study section assignment (within ~2 days of viewing window), notification of study section review date (scheduled ~4–5 months after deadline), Overall Impact Score or Percentile (within ~3 days of meeting), and Summary Statement release (within 30 days of meeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may also receive requests for post-submission materials. Know the expected timing for planning outreach to Program Officers and for resubmission decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment & Decision Steps After an Unsuccessful Review
rubrics_metrics.description: When not funded, applicants should (1) assess the summary statement to determine if problems are fixable and whether the right study section reviewed the application, (2) consult Program Officers about funding prospects and clarification of critiques, and (3) decide whether revision is worthwhile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision points include: Were the reviewers the right experts? Was the rationale and methods understood? Is the work fundamentally unexciting or unsalvageable? No amount of revising can fix deal-breaking flaws (e.g., unexciting topic, unsound hypothesis, methods unsuitable). Most grants require multiple submissions; plan revisions based on critiques and PI/discussion with program staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Fixable Problems (and solutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical remediable issues include poor writing/formatting/presentation, insufficient information/experimental details/preliminary data, significance not convincingly stated, research not shown to be feasible by proposed staff, and insufficient discussion of obstacles/alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested solutions: rewrite and get help with editing/formatting; add missing experimental details and data to the Research Plan; explicitly state importance to the IC mission and public health; recruit collaborators/consultants with needed expertise; describe contingency plans, decision trees, and alternative approaches to address negative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard-to-fix Problems (issues that may render resubmission futile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems that are often not fixable or require major overhaul include low-impact research topic, philosophical disagreements about importance, hypotheses that are unsound or unsupported by data, work already done, or methods unsuitable to test hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the core idea is judged unimportant or invalid, revision may not salvage the application; consider whether a different research question or stronger preliminary data are needed before resubmission.
